correctness.rationale: Every layer has occupancy 0, 1, or q, with a necessary-and-sufficient local domination condition. The unique run/full-piece decomposition gives exact length and weight formulas. For a full-piece word, the potential 3w-2n is at least 5 in all nonexceptional cases, whereas the constructed singleton optimum has potential at most 4. The only possible boundary exception E,F,E is optimum precisely at n=q=3. Weak compositions and adjacent-distinct run colors count the remaining minimizers exactly; for q=2 the graph is two disjoint paths, whose minimum maximal independent set gap count is binomial. The standalone graph-constructed brute-force checker examined every set of cardinality at most predicted minimum in 27 small cases; a separately implemented row DP agreed in 553 further cases. Numerical evidence supplements, not replaces, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source paper made independent domination of path--clique direct products a specifically studied graph-product problem, but left the number and classification of optimizers unresolved in its statements. The new theorem gives every optimal set, separates the q=2 disconnected case, explains an isolated full-layer exceptional optimum, and exhibits exponential dependence on clique size and path length at fixed minimum cardinality. The infinite-family structural rigidity and closed enumerator are natural, useful mathematical data rather than a small numerical improvement.
